craft_claim: Compressing an idea into an aphoristic unit makes it memorable and provokes interpretation, but an uninterrupted run of such units disintegrates the argument.

supporting_evidence.note: Hui argues the aphorism is the shortest literary form, at once open and closed, standing before, against, and after philosophy; minimal size is charged with maximal intensity and demands interpretation.
Bacon's essays are built around condensed, sententious closes that fix a general truth in the memory, ranging from plain statement to epigram.
Establishes the aphoristic and epigrammatic character of Bacon's prose as a documented stylistic feature.

scope: Essay, blog, copy and poetic-prose forms that need portable formulations of ideas.
exceptions: Aphorism stacking — consecutive unglossed maxims — is a failure mode, not a mechanism (see clm-tone-philosophical-pseudo-profundity).
